title: Review shared artifact, cache, IO, bundle, and serialization module families
scope: Primary ownership for src/shared artifact, cache, IO, bundle, and serialization helpers assigned to #411 in the shared-module ledger.

summary.overallAssessment: This shared surface is broadly useful and already owns many of the repo's right low-level seams, but it is too flat. The main cleanup opportunities are the oversized artifact-manifest and loader stack, the bundle persistence stack, the overlap between file helpers and atomic persistence helpers, the cache family layering story, and specialized metadata or contract wrappers that should move out of the generic storage/serialization bucket.

clusterFindings.assessment: This family is valuable and correctly shared, but manifest.js and the larger loader modules are carrying too many responsibilities at once. Manifest path safety, compatibility routing, shard layout, and fallback behavior are all coupled together, while the core loader surface mixes source resolution, materialization policy, and artifact-specific adapters.

The bundle and persistence family has the right shared ownership, but bundle-io.js and atomic-persistence.js are too broad. The current layering mixes format contract enforcement, worker offload, patching, checksums, backup swap logic, long-path handling, and retry policy in files that are hard to reason about.

The repo has the right primitives for cache policy, addressing, roots, and JSON-backed cache reads, but the story is not obvious from the paths alone. cache.js mixes byte estimation and in-memory LRU mechanics, cache-cas.js owns several distinct CAS concerns in one file, and cache-root and cache-key boundaries should be documented more explicitly.

These helpers are all legitimate shared surfaces, but files.js and json-stream.js have become catch-all facades. files.js now spans path predicates, read-range helpers, existence probes, and JSON safety helpers. json-stream.js similarly bundles array/object writing, sharded JSONL, offsets, compression, and temp-dir replacement orchestration.

The contract and metadata helpers that did not belong in this bucket have now moved out. The remaining specialized concern here is provenance metadata, which is coherent but should stay clearly bounded so additional contract or metadata surfaces do not drift back into the generic storage family.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: The file mixes manifest loading, path safety, compatibility routing, sidecar inference, and fallback policy in one oversized shared module.
The file currently owns bundle format handling, patching, checksum generation, worker offload, and locking logic. It should keep a facade but shed internal families.
Temp-path generation, rename retries, backup swap semantics, long-path handling, and EXDEV fallback behavior deserve narrower internal seams.
This is the broadest file in the family by consumer count and is now a mixed surface for path predicates, bounded JSON reads, and file-range primitives.
The file combines cache layer descriptors, byte estimators, cache reporters, and LRU construction. A smaller layering story would make reuse safer.
The json-stream family still mixes sharded JSONL orchestration, stream lifecycle, compression, and output coordination behind one broad facade.
